notes: Identity independently checked in supplied text: title including The Sexualized-Body-Inversion Hypothesis subtitle, all five authors, Psychological Science 23 (2012), pp. 469–471, and DOI 10.1177/0956797611434748 agree with original reference. This is a primary article with Method, Results and Discussion, references and supplemental analyses/pretest details, not merely an abstract. Header describes an author-uploaded full-text web rendering. No PDF was supplied; layout could not be checked. Canonical text contains OCR/line-break artifacts. Four candidates, with no selection: male upright versus inverted t(77) = 6.29, p < .001; female upright versus inverted t(77) = 1.38, p = .17; inverted female versus male t(77) = 5.42, p < .001; upright male versus female t(77) = 0.54, p = .59. Each p belongs to its own printed t. The broad post hoc description and locator do not distinguish these tests. Objects are a theoretical recognition comparison, not a third measured stimulus category. Method reports 78 recruited university students (41 men, 37 women), but does not explicitly identify mutually exclusive final analytic groups for the critical model or document exclusions. No analytic N is inferred from df or summed from recruitment groups. The interaction F(1, 75) and post hoc t(77) are preserved as printed; differing dfs do not establish a common analytic sample.
